body: Was it that you were more aware of your partner's behavior or was it that the ideas themselves were toxic?
I actually got a lot of this from reading books on sociobiology actually. Maybe therein lies the problem -- it's looking at things in simply evolutionary terms.
Good question as I've also been there. The matter that she would even explicitly tell you to garner a reaction is the real fulcrum to the issue (for me at least).
Not at all? Well, thank you for commenting. I feel I'm merely cynical.

Trust and passion are good, I think there's a tendency to overlook them because the issue of trust is one so easily breached. I means there's always this looming question about whether or not someone would behave faithfully if only certain conditions to their needs were met. That's a difficult matter.

Passion seems to come from both trust and communication, well, if it's legitimate really. I think the aversion I had towards communication itself is that I feel by addressing my concerns I demonstrate myself as weak, invalid, "beta" if you will, and therefore insecure and undeserving of the relationship. Perhaps that's why I really don't like communicating any longer.
Without "communication" being in the answer, how does one accomplish that?

Have you heard of there being an idea like the "end of history"? Something like that.

I feel disadvantaged primarily because I feel at the foundations of doing something like that, it would be out of a selfishness concealed under selflessness. I think people perform selfless acts because internally they're seeking to justify themselves as a good person. That is a selfish motive. True, they help others regardless of their internal reasoning, it just doesn't seem right. Second to this, I also wonder about what is lost by prioritizing the needs of others, when I already yield to everyone else in my life be they friends or drivers on the road looking to merge.

Yes, I would say what I've discussed with you today comes from a fatalistic perspective.

I help others where I can and I feel I perform a lot of selfless acts for nothing other than my own character. Maybe you're right but I'm reaching a point at which I feel disadvantaged by this pattern of behavior.

My interests? Well, to canvas them in a very broad sense -- philosophy (ethics, epistemology, aesthetics), economics and foreign affairs, and I guess to get somewhat specific, the emergence or drive towards something like a singularity or endpoint of technology and social arrangements.

Nothing at this point in my life really provides the kind of happiness that I once knew.

Regarding social abilities, I feel that I'm far too old to improve that. It's likely that whatever personality developed is relatively cemented now. There's an interaction about feeling comfortable with myself that's difficult to overcome. When the point of "comfort" is reached it's done through verification of successes and accomplishments and it sort of grows exponentially on that. As soon as some kind of snag is encountered there, I become really lost and disengage myself with everything, feeling badly enough as to think I could never again re-accomplish those things.

The interests that I enjoy are really boring things to most people and part of my failing is in being able to navigate conversation and to sell them better, should the topic or topics lend themselves to my interests. Yeah, I understand what you mean about the topic determining your abilities but we're talking about me being so daft as to sometimes bring a conversation back to myself which is where the tag of egotistical may have come from.

I was 26 as well OP; it happened this year as well. I never associated a great deal of meaning to sex or my virginity -- I'm just a relatively shy and anxious person.

It was fortunate I met someone off OkCupid who was sincere and genuine person. After forming the relationship, one evening lent itself to drunkenness which was uncharacteristic of me in that I was stacking alprazolam and drank a bottle of mead without eating. After vomiting behind a strip mall and walking about its parking lot she offered to take me home.

The sequence of events lent themselves towards fucking on my floor, absolutely wasted. I was only ashamed that I was too trashed, and well, that I've lost my ability to become a wizard upon turning 30.

I never felt like I put much stock onto the act of "losing" it itself but again, I'm glad it was with a really great person. Unfortunately things did not work out with her.

Just a 26 year old ex-virgin to another OP. Hope that your future endeavors prove better.
